result.summary: The page is generally coherent, but a few visual/usability issues stand out: horizontally scrolling content is clipped at the right edge, some secondary text has low contrast, and small icon-only controls may be hard to use.

issues.description: The right edge shows partially clipped category/restaurant items, including a sliver of a chip after “Healthy” and the “Trattoria Piccol…” card being cut off mid-name.
issues.suggestion: Add clearer carousel affordances such as edge fade, page dots, or adjusted card spacing so intentionally off-screen items look deliberate rather than broken.

issues.description: Search placeholder text “Restaurants, dishes, groceries” appears light gray on a light background and may be difficult to read for low-vision users.
issues.suggestion: Increase placeholder contrast or use a darker gray that meets WCAG contrast guidance while still looking secondary.

issues.description: The notification bell and favorite heart controls are icon-only and relatively small, which can make their purpose and hit targets less accessible.
issues.suggestion: Provide accessible labels and ensure touch targets are at least about 44x44 pt with sufficient contrast.

issues.description: Secondary metadata such as delivery fees and time ranges uses pale gray text that may be hard to scan quickly, especially over light card backgrounds.
issues.suggestion: Darken secondary text slightly or increase font weight to improve readability without changing the visual hierarchy.
